newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's ANC seeks to quash succession doubts.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's ANC seeks to quash succession doubts.

text.p: South Africa's ruling African National Congress sought on Monday to quash speculation over who would succeed President Nelson Mandela, saying the leader of the powerful Johannesburg-based branch of the party would not contest the post.

"The African National Congress in Gauteng wants to put on record that Comrade Tokyo Sexwale will not be available for the position of presidency of the country nor will he be available for the deputy president's position in 1999," a statement from the ANC in Gauteng province said.

"The ANC in Gauteng fully supports this move by Sexwale and is sure that it will put a stop to all speculation that he will contest the position of presidency against Comrade Thabo Mbeki," the statement said.

It was issued following newspaper reports that Sexwale had been responsible for leaks from a top level ANC meeting eight days ago to the effect that Mandela had declined to specifically endorse Mbeki as his successor.
Mandela, due to stand down in 1999, has spoken warmly of Mbeki as someone who would be well-suited for the job. But he has said the final decision will be made by a national conference of the ANC.
He dismissed media reports, based on quotes from an unnamed source at the November 10 meeting, that he appeared to be distancing himself from Mbeki.
Political commentators have suggested that Sexwale, who is premier of Gauteng province, and Mbeki, who is deputy president, are rivals for power within the ANC.
The ANC statement said the Gauteng branch, representing Pretoria and the industrial-commercial hub of Johannesburg, would urge Sexwale to serve another term as premier of the province.
